notes: Reference: a creator reel in the #cornersofmyhome / #cozyvibes register (jklmnest, 'you can never have too many lamps'). Genre conventions only — the reference video was never visible to the session, so the grade is this system's aesthetic style, not a measured match. Its own track (music6-corners, ElevenLabs eleven_music_v2, 900 credits) rather than the shared music1-aesthetic, because every other aesthetic-style reel already uses that one; measured at 71.8 BPM by system/beatgrid.py, so the cut is 1.672 s, not 1.766. Nine corners, four fixtures, two shots each, walked in one evening: aurora hall -> cube living -> teak dining -> rosewood evening -> cube bedside -> aurora bedroom -> teak underside detail -> rosewood endcap macro -> cube console at Diwali. Half the pendant photography was shot in daylight (mean luminance 186-192 vs 36-90 for the night frames), so those four shots carry a per-shot evening grade and the one very dark teak frame is lifted; measured, not eyeballed. Film grain cut from alls=5 to 2 because grain through a 0.35 s dissolve blows out. No price, no proof line, no CTA screen before the end card — a save/share cut, judged on saves. Second pass: the teak night frame (mean 36) read as a dead black 1.8 s on the sheet and the contained rosewood dining frame as an empty letterbox, so both were replaced with lit wood details — it also gives the cut two macros against seven wides instead of nine wides.
